Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the asks we committed to:

- What HealthBridge needs: confirmation of exactly what prompt input and model-generated output Redwood persists, where those records are stored (region), and default retention windows for both hosted and private deployments.
- You also asked about logging controls (what goes into debug logs), access controls for stored outputs, and how we support prompt minimization (token masking) for PII.

Action items I promised:
1) Provide a concise one-pager saying for hosted API: which fields are ephemeral vs persisted, default TTLs, and encryption-at-rest locations.
2) Share the retention_matrix_v2.xlsx that maps each artifact (raw prompt, structured fields, model output, KV cache snapshots, debug logs) to default TTL and access policy.
3) Loop in Marcus (security) and Dev (engineering) for any technical exceptions or hosting-territory requests.

Summary of our default positions (high level):
- Hosted (redwood.com endpoints): prompts and outputs are stored for 30 days by default for quality/abuse monitoring.
- Customers can opt into ephemeral-only mode (0 retention on prompt and output) for select routes when on an enterprise plan + Private or Dedicated offering.
- Debug/trace logs are sampled and redacted by default; full debug is only enabled with customer consent and is TTL-limited.

I'll attach the one-pager and retention matrix. If you want a firm commitment for HIPAA-covered workflows or a custom TTL <30 days for hosted, we should plan a short security call next week to scope SOC2 artifacts and a contract amendment.

We prefer to have those technical answers in writing before we share the PII scoping doc with our legal/compliance team. Can you please confirm?

Elena — great questions. Short answers below; Marcus and Dev will expand where needed.

1) Storage location and access:
- Hosted API: persisted prompt/outputs live in Redwood's encrypted control-plane storage (customer-scoped). By default the data is stored in the region where the customer's account is provisioned (we showed US-west today).
- Operational access: only a limited set of Redwood SRE/ops engineers have audited access via IAM roles; access is logged and requires justification. We enforce RBAC and time-bound access for incident investigations.

2) Ephemeral-only mode scope:
- We support an ephemeral policy option that prevents raw prompts, outputs, and KV cache snapshots from being written to persisted storage.
- Note: ephemeral mode still maintains in-memory KV cache for the duration of a session for latency; no persistent snapshots are created when ephemeral is enabled.

3) PII redaction in debug logs:
- Redwood performs automated redaction for common PII patterns (SSN-like sequences, emails, phone numbers).
- For custom schemas (structured PHI fields you consider sensitive), we can accept a JSON schema/field list and apply token masking before logs are written. This is typically part of the Private/Dedicated onboarding or an enterprise addendum for hosted.

Next steps: Marcus will confirm the default TTLs and provide wording suitable for inclusion in your compliance packet. Can Marcus supply a short paragraph we can include in the SOW?

Thanks,
Naomi

Hi Elena — Marcus here (Security). Per Naomi's note, below is the language we can use in the compliance packet / SOW. Please let me know if you'd like this as a PDF/slide.

Official wording (suitable for SOW):
"Redwood will, by default, retain customer prompt inputs and model-generated outputs in encrypted storage for 30 days for the hosted API. Customers may elect an ephemeral retention profile for specific API routes or account-wide where prompt inputs, model outputs, and persisted KV cache snapshots are not written to durable storage (session-only in-memory KV retained for active sessions). Debug and trace logs are sampled and redacted by default; Redwood will apply automated pattern-based redaction for common PII and can accept customer-supplied field lists for additional masking as part of an enterprise onboarding. Operational access to persisted prompt/output data is restricted to a small set of audited Redwood personnel via RBAC and requires justification; all access is logged and retained for 90 days. For customers requiring sub-30-day retention or local data residency guarantees, Redwood offers Dedicated or Private deployment options with contractual retention terms and region-specific data residency enforcement."

Additional technical notes (for your engineers):
- TTLs for hosted control-plane objects: prompts/outputs = 30d, sampled debug traces = 90d (sampled), audit access logs = 90d.
- Ephemeral mode: no write to object store; in-memory KV only while session active.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit; customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments.

If that looks good I can convert to a one-page PDF and drop into the DocuSign SOW draft Naomi mentioned.

Regards,
